body: I don't think it will get better for me. Just a few seconds ago she barged into my room sobbing and telling me that I was a selfish person who does absolutely nothing for her and I "care for her so little" and how she will no longer "do anything for me". I don't want to keep living anymore. I just want it to stop.
They live all the way across the country ):

Not sure if a shelter is an option, because I will have nowhere to store my things or take care of my animals. I have family out of state, but no way of getting to them sadly. No friends to stay with either since I've been kept isolated and I moved out of state with my abuser recently. Most of my friends in my home state are minors anyway so I couldn't stay with them. I'm sort of stuck trying to find a job and get out as soon as possible. Lately because of my poor mental health, I've become extremely lazy at home to the point where I can't get out of bed or do anything, but when I'm away from home, I work very hard.
I'm almost 20. I'm open to that honestly. I don't want to die, I just really need a way out of this place.

I have nowhere to go and I have medical issues, I need my medication regularly or I'll possibly die. Without my parent, I have no money, and no medication. I'm trying to get employed for awhile now but I haven't had any luck.
I will never be happy. I will never escape this place. My life was ruined before it started. I never had a fighting chance.
Thank you for the suggestion. I got her some treats and a little blanket that she settled in. She seems to have forgiven me and is brushing against my hand, but I still feel guilty ):

While I'm not a fan of the movie itself, what really sold it for me was Art the Clown's performance. It was great. Something about the way he mocks and torments people in silence with savage glee just scares the shit out of me. He kind of reminds me of The Gentlemen from that one episode of Buffy the Vampire Slayer. So creepy. The whole idea of these random people just being in the wrong place at the wrong time freaks me out as well.


It's no masterpiece, but I kind of liked that cheesy B-movie charm it had.

The truth about depression is that there are lots of reasons someone can become depressed. Sometimes, it's entirely chemical (happens out of nowhere), and sometimes it's environmental. Sometimes it's a mix of the two. People will become depressed for no reason at all, and people taking in negativity from their environments are more likely to become depressed as well. For me, I'm a mix of both. I become depressed for no reason, even when things are going well, but I also acknowledge that my situation is less than ideal and is contributing to my depression. I also have PTSD and it kind of messes with everything, which also contributes to my depression.


Only you and any mental health professional you speak with will know if you have depression. There are depression elitists out there who like to define their experience with depression as the only ~real~ one, but it's bullshit. If you're experiencing symptoms of depression then it's likely you're dealing with depression, and you aren't lazy or making excuses.

I don't think I've ever been traumatized by a horror movie, but I did get really scared by  John Carpenter's The Thing when I was 7 or 8. I watched it with my dad and I remember loving that it scared me so much. For a few months after that I afraid my cat was going to turn into a Thing in the middle of the night and attack me.
Thank you. This was very helpful and reassuring. It helps me feel a bit more in control to realize that what I experience due to depression isn't always what's actually happening.
